channel.title: Net Sense
channel.description: Studio network monitoring for Mac, by Nathaniel Labs.

item.description:
# Net Sense 1.8.10
How long a line's data lasts is now judged by the last full week, so a refill is not shown as lasting longer than it will.
- Run-out date uses the last seven full days

# Net Sense 1.8.9
A new Usage screen shows what each line is carrying right now, data used today and this week, data left including refills, and puts a YouTube upload, a download or ChatGPT on a chosen line.
- Live speed per line and the devices using it this moment - GB per day for the last week, coloured by line - Data left this month, counting refills bought on top of the plan - Who used the data: school devices and apps on the studio Mac - Start a YouTube upload window, a download window or ChatGPT on the line you pick

# Net Sense 1.8.8
Any app can now be given its own internet line.
- Each line is offered as a local door. Point an app at the ACT door and only that app leaves by ACT, while everything else stays on Jio. Proved with Codex: twelve requests to chatgpt.com, all out via ACT. - A line's lane is refused rather than silently offered when this Mac does not hold that line's address, so an app is never pointed at a door that goes nowhere. - Going back to the usual line now names the line that recovered, instead of the one being left. - Falling back to a line that has already spent its month's data now says so.

# Net Sense 1.8.7
Both lines now carry Jio's real 3,300 GB limit, and a line is rated on the days it was actually watched.
- Jio's own postpaid tariff document, clause 6, sets a commercial usage threshold of 3,300 GB a billing cycle and stops the data past it. That limit is now on record for Jio, with the document it came from. - A line's rate is taken over the days it was actually counted, not the whole billing month. Jio read 98 GB a day while it was moving over 400. - When a line's limit falls inside the billing month, the panel names the day it runs out.

# Net Sense 1.8.6
Fixes the new plan settings, which could not be saved in 1.8.5.
- A line's data limit, reset day and the bill it came from now save properly.

# Net Sense 1.8.5
Each line now carries its real plan, and data is counted against that plan's own billing month.
- Jio bills from the 11th to the 10th. Usage is measured over that window now, not the calendar month. - A line's monthly allowance, reset day, speed, price and the bill each came from are kept with the line. - Where there is no limit on record the panel says so, instead of showing nothing. - A line can be anchored to the provider's own usage figure so the total matches the bill.

# Net Sense 1.8.4
The whole network can be put on one line, and Net Sense now counts how much data each line and device uses.
- One switch sends everything out by Jio or ACT, with the other line kept as automatic backup. - Devices pinned on the Devices page still win over that switch. - Data used this month now shows on the Lines page, against each plan's monthly allowance. - Warns at 50%, 80% and 95% of a plan's data limit, instead of after it runs out.

# Net Sense 1.8.3
Net Sense now moves this Mac off an internet line that stops being usable, instead of waiting for it to go dead.
- A line is judged on whether a lesson would survive it, not on the router's up/down flag: 4% packet loss, 150 ms latency or 80 ms of timing swing is enough to call it unusable. - When the line a device is pinned to goes bad and the other line is healthy, Net Sense moves the device itself within one probe cycle and says why. - It moves back to your chosen line only after that line has been steady for about ten minutes, refuses to move onto a line that is also bad, and stops moving if both lines are flapping. - The routing panel shows each line's live verdict, the last move made, and an on/off switch. - A routing rule is now named after the line it actually uses.

# Net Sense 1.8.2
Connect new laptops to school Wi-Fi first, then optionally open Net Sense.
- Windows, Mac, Chromebook and Linux Wi-Fi computers can use the school network name and password without an existing internet connection. - Connect a device now shows laptop Wi-Fi details and the phone Wi-Fi QR before dashboard access. - Copy invitation creates a fresh read-only link using the numeric LAN address, with no short-name discovery or code typing required.

# Net Sense 1.8.1
Recognise your devices and open the master Net Sense on a laptop more easily.
- Devices now show the available model and operating system beside the person; confirmed device names are remembered by the master. - Share Net Sense puts the laptop link, real Mac clipboard copy and AirDrop sharing in one place. - Enrol a laptop once to keep access when its private Wi-Fi address changes; no separate router login is needed.

# Net Sense 1.8.0
Laptops can now join Net Sense, and Net Sense now keeps itself up to date.
- On a laptop, type netsense.local:8796 and the code from Add device. - Every Mac running Net Sense installs new versions by itself within 30 minutes.

# Net Sense 1.7.4
Opens correctly in older Safari, and still installs on Intel Macs and macOS 11 and newer.
- The certificate check now tells the truth on Macs that are not this studio machine. - The app remains a universal Intel + Apple Silicon binary for macOS 11 Big Sur and newer. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.7.3
The current Net Sense now installs on Intel Macs and on macOS 11 Big Sur and newer.
- The app and the engine are universal Intel + Apple Silicon binaries. - The minimum system version is macOS 11.0, which is the oldest macOS that can host this WebKit app. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.5.1
The installer now opens on Intel Macs and on macOS 11 Big Sur and newer, not only Apple Silicon Ventura.
- The app and the engine are universal Intel + Apple Silicon binaries. - The minimum system version is macOS 11.0, which is the oldest macOS that can host this WebKit app. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.5.0
Every connected host can now have its own internet preference, speed cap, and school identity.
- Tap a device to prefer ACT or Jio for that host, with automatic fallback on the other line. - Set a download and upload speed cap per host, then read the live rate and session totals back from the controller. - NSM-owned systems are recognised separately from people, including the Mac running Net Sense. - The new-user QR stays single-use, expires in five minutes, and points at this Mac on Nathaniel School Wi-Fi. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.4.0
Watchtower turns provider failures into dependable, restrained alerts and outage evidence.
- ACT, Jio, and any future provider are confirmed independently, including a line that was already down when Net Sense opened. - A single-line failure confirms after about 30 seconds; a total outage escalates faster; recovery waits for 60 stable seconds. - The signed Net Sense app now delivers native Mac banners, a two-tone outage alarm, a softer recovery chime, Dock badges, and green/amber/red menu-bar status. - A persistent in-app banner keeps the fault visible while “Acknowledge sound” silences reminders without hiding the outage. - Watchtower settings show notification readiness, safe Mac alert testing, optional Keychain-backed Brevo staff email, exact email previews, timings, current incidents, and delivery history. - The new clock button builds an instant ACT and Jio report for 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days: total downtime, current outage duration, incident count, longest outage, availability, and recorded evidence coverage. - Monitoring gaps are excluded rather than guessed, so time while Net Sense was not running can never be misreported as provider downtime. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.3.1
The scorecard wording now agrees with the live evidence.
- Cards with thousands of reachability and Omada samples say that operational monitoring is live instead of incorrectly saying there are no measurements. - A withheld throughput grade is labelled “not graded,” not “provisional score.” - All live statistics and outage separation from 1.3.0 are unchanged. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.3.0
The live ISP statistics are useful again without running disruptive speed tests.
- Omada's direct WAN state now records confirmed line availability and observed downtime separately for ACT and Jio. - The lightweight 30-second probes now produce median and p95 latency, jitter, packet loss, reply availability, and represented no-reply time instead of being discarded from the scorecard. - A controller-confirmed line outage is no longer mixed up with an unverified routed-path failure, so Net Sense does not blame an ISP without the right evidence. - Throughput and bufferbloat remain clearly historical and ungraded while automatic bandwidth-saturating tests are off. - An app left open now checks for updates every six hours and opens the current notarized installer directly, while avoiding repeated prompts for the same version. - The release build now refuses a non-portable Python engine before it can reach another Mac. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.2.3
Security release. One gap found by attacking the running app from the studio network, and closed.
- A page on a malicious website could previously confirm Net Sense was running on your network and read back what it was doing, by pretending to be a site your browser already trusted. It could not reach anything private — every page, device list and Wi-Fi code still required an enrolled device — but there was no reason to answer it at all. It is now refused. - Net Sense also no longer reports its internal process number to anyone who asks. - Everything else held up under attack: made-up access codes, guessed codes, codes copied into a web address, and every attempt to change a setting from an unenrolled phone were all rejected. - Your Wi-Fi password and staff details are never written to this Mac in readable form; they stay in the Mac's own Keychain. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.2.2
Sharing the studio Wi-Fi finally works.
- The guest Wi-Fi QR now builds itself. Net Sense is already signed in to the Omada controller, so it reads the school's network name and password straight from the router — nothing to type, and the code works the first time you ask for it. - Both QR codes can now leave this Mac. Share opens the Mac share sheet for AirDrop, Messages, Mail or WhatsApp; Save writes the picture to Downloads and shows it in Finder. Previously the buttons did nothing at all, silently, because a Mac app's web view has no downloads or share sheet of its own. - The Wi-Fi sheet says out loud that anyone who receives the picture can join. The team enrolment sheet says the opposite: that code only works on school Wi-Fi, and only for five minutes. - When something is refused, Net Sense now shows its own plain-English reason instead of a line like "/api/wifi-qr?network=main → 400". - An enterprise (802.1X) network is told it cannot become a QR, rather than producing a code that could never work. - A momentary controller failure keeps the last good answer instead of erasing a QR that was working a second ago. - The Power page names the router by model (ER7212PC) instead of showing its raw MAC address. - Closes a dependency security advisory, and the engine now runs on a maintained Python with its own current security libraries. - Signed with Jason Zac's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.

# Net Sense 1.2.1
Live telemetry and security hardening release.
- Team devices can no longer read the studio Wi-Fi password or staff phone numbers; the Wi-Fi QR now needs the Operator role. - Quitting or crashing the app can never leave the engine running unnoticed on the network. - An idle phone can no longer appear to be downloading at its radio link rate; unknown readings show as blanks instead of invented numbers. - A controller hiccup keeps the previous reading and says so, instead of wiping the lines while claiming to be live. - Replaces the disruptive on-demand speed tests with always-on live per-line telemetry: each WAN card now shows what the line is actually doing right now, continuously. - Restores the verified Omada session login, so the controller connection is authenticated the proven way again. - Clarifies roaming and device trust: a phone moving between access points is no longer mistaken for a new device. - Closes all outstanding dependency security advisories; the release now passes its own security audit gate. - Signed with Jason's Developer ID and accepted and stapled by Apple's notarization service.
